subsystems.name: Ultra-high-vacuum growth chamber
subsystems.role: keeps the growing crystal free of contamination — even a stray gas molecule would spoil the layer.

subsystems.name: Source cells
subsystems.role: evaporate each element at a precisely controlled rate.
parts: effusion (Knudsen) cells for metals like gallium
cracker cells for arsenic and phosphorus
radio-frequency plasma source for nitrogen or oxygen

subsystems.name: Substrate stage
subsystems.role: holds and heats the wafer, and rotates it for uniform growth.
parts: radiative heater and thermocouple or pyrometer

subsystems.name: Shutters and process control
subsystems.role: start and stop each beam in a fraction of a second, which is how single atomic layers are built.

subsystems.name: In-situ metrology
subsystems.role: watches the surface while it grows, so layer thickness is counted rather than guessed.

subsystems.name: Ex-situ finishing
subsystems.role: turns the grown wafer into devices.

buildSteps.title: Prepare the substrate
buildSteps.detail: A polished single-crystal wafer is degreased, etched and mounted on a holder with indium or a graphite clamp so heat transfers evenly.

buildSteps.title: Reach ultra-high vacuum
buildSteps.detail: The chamber is baked for hours to drive off water and hydrocarbons, reaching pressures around 10^-10 millibar — roughly a trillionth of atmospheric pressure.

buildSteps.title: Clean the surface
buildSteps.detail: The wafer is heated to several hundred degrees Celsius under a beam of the volatile element (arsenic or phosphorus) to desorb its oxide and leave an atomically flat, ordered surface, confirmed by RHEED.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate the beams
buildSteps.detail: Each source is warmed to its working temperature and its flux measured so the growth rate is known to within a fraction of an atomic layer per second.

buildSteps.title: Grow the layered stack
buildSteps.detail: Shutters open and close in sequence while the substrate rotates, depositing one atomic layer at a time; temperature and flux changes set the alloy composition and built-in strain.

buildSteps.title: Form three-dimensional features
buildSteps.detail: For quantum dots, strain is deliberately allowed to build until the film breaks into nanoscale islands; for nanowires or site-controlled dots, the wafer is pre-patterned so growth happens only in defined holes. This is where true 3D control is hardest.

buildSteps.title: Anneal and cap
buildSteps.detail: A short anneal improves crystal quality and a thin protective cap layer stops the surface oxidising once the wafer leaves vacuum.

buildSteps.title: Process into devices
buildSteps.detail: Standard semiconductor fabrication — lithography, etching, contacts — converts the structure into lasers, transistors or detectors.

buildSteps.title: Characterise
buildSteps.detail: Photoluminescence, X-ray diffraction and electron microscopy confirm layer thickness, composition and defect density before the wafer is released.

prerequisites.why: without pressures near 10^-10 millibar, residual gas poisons the crystal as it grows.
source purity sets the purity of the finished crystal; there is no later purification step.
the grown layers copy the atomic template beneath them, defects and all.
RHEED oscillations let operators count atomic layers and stop precisely where they intend.
self-assembled quantum dots land at random positions; site-controlled growth works in the lab but not yet reliably across a full wafer.
MBE grows at roughly a micrometre per hour or less, far slower than chemical vapour deposition, so it stays a specialty tool.

pathway.unlocks: lasers, high-electron-mobility transistors, infrared detectors and low-noise electronics that other methods cannot match.

pathway.milestone: site-controlled quantum dots and nanowires on patterned wafers
pathway.unlocks: single-photon sources and qubits that can be addressed individually, because each one sits where the design puts it.

pathway.milestone: routine van der Waals heterostructures and 2D-material stacks
pathway.unlocks: ultrathin devices built from dissimilar layers that would never combine in bulk crystal.

pathway.milestone: hybrid atomic-scale manufacturing, pairing MBE with lithography or probe-based atom manipulation
pathway.unlocks: genuinely three-dimensional atomic precision over useful areas — the idea this label points at, but not yet a production reality.
